title: Native Lean finite Nash equilibria
abstract: Formalizes finite strategic-form games with player-specific finite move sets, pure profiles, unilateral deviations, best responses, dominant strategies, and two distinct potential notions. Pure Nash equilibrium is defined over utility preorders by the absence of a strict improvement; weak-inequality characterizations are restricted to linear orders. The library names the one-way improvement condition a generalized ordinal potential and reserves ordinal potential for the standard bidirectional strict-sign condition. It proves a global potential-maximizer certificate for pure Nash equilibrium, the standard Nash/local-potential-maximum equivalence, and acyclicity of the better-response relation for the generalized class. The development also gives checked counterexamples and Prisoner's-Dilemma/coordination/matching-pennies/rock-paper-scissors examples. Its native mixed layer proves support equalization, Dirac transport, the normalized excess-map reduction, and the closed/compact/ convex/continuous finite mixed-profile geometry. It also proves general finite mixed-Nash existence on a common nonempty move type by connecting the native excess map to an attributed, kernel-checked product-of-simplices Brouwer theorem. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics or the first Lean proof of Nash existence.
